newsitem.title: USA: AIG seeks to overturn Golden Eagle decision.
newsitem.headline: AIG seeks to overturn Golden Eagle decision.

text.p: American International Group Inc said it will take all steps necessary to overturn the results of a court-supervised auction in California Friday that awarded workers' compensation insurer Golden Eagle to Liberty Mutual Group.

The California insurance department in April said American International had won the bidding for Golden Eagle, which was seized by the department in late January because of allegations of a reserve shortfall.
The state's agreement with AIG was subject to court review.

But AIG said the court's decision disregarded the results of a sealed-bid auction conducted by Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush, which AIG won, and further disregarded definitive agreements entered into with the insurance department reflecting that winning bid.

"The Department of Insurance failed to defend its statutory bidding process, its decision to award the bid and its contractual obligations with AIG as the winning bidder," AIG executive vice president Robert Sandler said.

"AIG has been working for months to insure that Golden Eagle's policyholders, employees and independent producers were not hurt by the (department of insurance's) rehabilitation proceedings," he said.
David Walsh, general counsel for AIG's domestic brokerage group, also criticized the action.
"The Department changed its position with no notice to AIG," Walsh said. "Policyholders, the industry and legislators have to be able to rely upon the commissioner's word," he said.

"How can the Department reverse its position with no prior notice and without any explanation," Walsh added. "AIG had faith in the process and invested substantial resources based on the commissioner's contractual commitments, he said.
Golden Eagle, a company valued at $1.3 billion, wrote about $400 million of workers compensation and $300 million of property-casualty business in 1996, according to the department of insurance.
The state's department of insurance said it seized Golden Eagle after its investigators turned up evidence the company had manipulated its financial records.
The rehabilitation of Golden Eagle has taken a number of twists over the last six months.

In early February, the insurance department reached an agreement in principle for the rehabilitation of Golden Eagle with Superior National Insurance Group Inc, Insurance Partners L.P and members of the Zurich Centre Group.

Several weeks later, after receiving expressions of interest from other companies, Quackenbush reached an agreement with Liberty Mutual in which it would back Golden Eagle policies and he issued a request for proposals for the rehabilitation plan for Golden Eagle.
In April, American International said it had been informed by the insurance department that it had won the bidding for Golden Eagle.
And in May, Quackenbush said he executed a definitive agreement with AIG, which set out the details of the rehabilitation plan for Golden Eagle.
AIG chairman Maurice Greenberg said AIG is committed to a strong and vigorous presence in California and has been expanding its operations in Southern California.
"We pursued Golden Eagle because it fit well with our ongoing strategy to develop our middle market business and increase our penetration in this segment of the industry," he said.
He said that "with or without Golden Eagle", AIG is committed to serving its clients in the middle market.
